sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and pronotum chestnut, abdominal tergites reddish brown, postclypeus and base of the mandibles paler than the head (Sudan brown), anteclypeus transparent, labrum, maxillary palps, antennae, legs and wing buds concolorous with the postclypeus, wings pale brown. Setae on the head very numerous, some distinctly longer than most; compound eyes hemispherical, not distinctly flattened above. Postclypeus large, distinctly raised, rounded behind and truncate in front, sparsely hairy; anteclypeus very long, almost as long as the postclypeus, wide at the base and abruptly narrowed to a pointed apex. Labrum large, about as long as wide, narrowed at the base, rounded at the sides and in front, widest in the middle, with several medium-length red setae, the sides and apex transparent. Antenna 14-segmented, segment 3 the smallest, segment 4 as long as segment 2 but wider and rounded, segment 5 smaller than segment 4. Ocelli medium-sized, broadly oval, the distance to the compound eyes less than their short diameter; compound eyes circular, medium-sized (diameter 0.187), the facets fine and dense, about as far from the lower margin of the head as the ocelli are from the compound eyes. Pronotum with very numerous setae, narrower than the head, the anterior margin wavy and slightly upturned, the anterolateral corners rounded, the sides oblique toward the posterior margin, the posterior margin wide and slightly wavy; the posterior margin of the meso- and metanotum distinctly wavy. Wings: the first two veins parallel, close together and dark; the remaining veins, except for the first 5—6 branches of the cubitus, indistinct but traceable to the wing margin; the wing margin densely ciliate, bare only on the posterior margin near the apical 1/3; the radial sector with numerous setae along its whole length; the media crosses slightly above the middle of the wing and reaches the margin near the apex, generally with 2—3 branches; the cubitus generally with 7 branches in the fore wing and 9—10 in the hind wing, the last branch generally subdivided. Legs short and moderately thick; abdomen long and slender, the tergites with as many setae as the former. Measurements: head length (to the tip of the labium) 0.85, head length (to the frontoclypeal suture) 0.57, head width 0.68, pronotum length 0.50, width 0.51, abdominal width 0.79 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: This paper adds only the soldier measurements: pronotum length 0.22, width 0.48, hind tibia length 0.47 mm; the length and width of the head and the mandible length are illegible in the scan of the original.

note: Adapted from the redescription by Hill (1927), the original description being in Hill 1915, original in English; the alate is described in full, the soldier only by supplementary measurements, and the worker is not described. Type locality Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia.
